strengths: Strong theoretical contributions: Theorem 1 elegantly shows IQ-Learn reduces to BC through clever re-parameterization; Theorem 2 establishes equivalence with AIL while maintaining non-adversarial optimization.
Clear identification of Bellman constraints as the key mechanism for avoiding compounding errors, with rigorous primal-dual framework derivation and intuitive explanations (e.g., C.4 example).
Addresses a fundamental question about algorithmic mechanisms in Q-based IL with concrete theorems and lower bounds (Ω(H²) for IQ-Learn).
Comprehensive analysis including detection of derivation gap in IQ-Learn (Appendix B.4) and backward induction proof showing Q-value propagation through Bellman constraints.
Experimental validation on both synthetic hard instance and MuJoCo, with results supporting theoretical predictions.
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 2 addresses constrained optimization (Eq. 8) but practical algorithm uses penalty-based regularization (Eq. 26); no analysis of how well penalties approximate constraints or guidance for choosing β.

Restrictive assumptions limit practical applicability: (i) Theorem 1 assumes softmax policy realizes BC—realizability may fail with limited function approximation; (ii) Proposition 1 requires TD MDPs (Definition 1) with unclear prevalence in real domains; (iii) Corollary 1 provides lower bound only for specific hard instance, not general characterization.

Limited experimental improvements: Figure 2 shows Dual Q-DM competitive with but not substantially better than state-of-the-art HyPE; modest improvements over Reg IQ-Learn which already uses online Bellman error regularization; only 5 MuJoCo tasks tested.

Unclear practical significance of main generalization result: No discussion of how to verify TD MDP conditions in practice, what fraction of domains satisfy them, or algorithm behavior when violated; Proposition 1's applicability is questionable.

Missing implementation details and sensitivity analysis: No guidance on β selection, no ablations on regularization strength, no computational cost comparison with baselines, no error bars in Figure 2.

strengths: Strong theoretical results: Theorem 1 rigorously proves IQ-Learn reduces to BC via elegant re-parameterization; Corollary 1 establishes O(H²) lower bound; Theorem 2 shows equivalence to AIL
Novel value flow mechanism: Insightful identification of how Bellman constraints enable generalization through Q-value propagation; well-motivated by TD-MDP assumption
Comprehensive theoretical framework: Rigorous primal-dual development from distribution matching to Q-functions; extends to infinite-horizon setting
Solid experimental validation: Hard instance directly demonstrates O(H²) vs O(H) gap; offline experiments corroborate Theorem 1; broad baseline comparisons
Clear presentation: Good motivation with concrete examples; effective use of remarks; well-organized with comprehensive appendix
weaknesses: Restrictive unvalidated assumptions: TD-MDP assumption (Prop. 1) not empirically verified on MuJoCo; realizability and deterministic expert policy assumed but not discussed; limits practical applicability

Theory-practice gap: Despite Theorem 1, empirical IQ-Learn substantially outperforms BC; official IQ-Learn implementation includes regularization absent from original paper, undermining empirical validation
Limited scope of lower bound: Corollary 1 uses artificial Reset Cliff instance; doesn't characterize when Ω(H²) is tight or predict performance on typical domains
Incomplete practical algorithm analysis: Penalized objective not guaranteed to find feasible solutions; no convergence analysis; unanalyzed approximation error in continuous control version (Eq. 28)
Modest empirical improvements: Figure 2 shows overlapping error bars; improvements over Reg IQ-Learn often marginal; computational cost not compared
Insufficient engagement with related methods: LS-IQ/ReCOIL also use Bellman regularization; why do they work if online interactions alone don't help? Limited explanation of differences
Incomplete experimental analysis: Very limited expert data (1-5 trajectories); no verification that MuJoCo satisfies TD-MDPs despite this being critical for theoretical guarantees
